title: New Airline or Tail Number Spotter Alert
dataSources: ADS-B aircraft snapshots (`adsb:aircraft`), personal flight logbook (`flight:log`), commute trips (`commute:trip`), transit arrivals (`transit:arrival`), geofence events (`geofence:event`), travel documents (`travel:document`), fare quotes (`airprice:quote`).
app: Home ADS-B receiver (dump1090 / readsb / tar1090 JSON feed), personal flight logbook exports, commute/transit APIs, and phone geofence webhooks via Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=adsb:aircraft
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen by hex callsign operator
| eval hours_since=round((now()-first_seen)/3600,1)
| where hours_since<24
| sort first_seen
description: Highlights newly seen operators or tail numbers in your own receiver history, turning the local ADS-B feed into a lightweight aircraft-spotting notebook.
value: Novelty is part of the fun in flight spotting; this lets the data tell you what was truly new instead of relying on memory.
implementation: Forward ADS-B snapshots with hex and operator identifiers; review newly seen aircraft daily or trigger a push for favourites.
visualization: Inventory table of aircraft first seen in the past 24 hours.
grandmaExplanation: It watches which planes or airlines showed up in your local sky for the first time recently.
